lesson.title: Working Through Lists
lesson.driving_question: How can a program display every item in a list and report how many items it has?
lesson.primary_concept_family: A for loop can visit each item in a list, while len() counts the items.
lesson.concept_budget: One loop shape and one counting function; do not add indexes or nested collections.
misconceptions: The loop variable takes one item at a time.
The indented line belongs to the loop.
The list name after in must be the collection being visited.
len(list) returns the number of items, not the last position.
lesson.progression_note: Lesson 10 created and changed a list. Lesson 11 gives the learner two safe ways to use it: display each item and count the collection.
code_expectations: no index arithmetic or nested loops

shared_program.code:
survey = ["tea", "water", "juice"]
for drink in survey:
    print("Drink:", drink)
print("Total drinks:", len(survey))
shared_program.expected_output:
Drink: tea
Drink: water
Drink: juice
Total drinks: 3

primm.prompt: Recall: How did Lesson 10 store several items? Which line adds one item? What does indentation show?
Without running the code, predict each line displayed by the loop and the final total. Explain which value drink has on each pass.
Run the supplied file. Compare the order and total with your prediction, then explain one match or mismatch.

questions: Why does the loop variable contain one list item rather than its numeric position?
In what order are tea, water and juice displayed, and what controls that order?
Why does len(survey) still display 3 after the loop, rather than counting all the letters in the drink names?

primm.prompt: Change the example so it counts the drinks as the loop runs. Store 0 in [visited] before the for loop and add 1 inside it. After the loop, display "Visited:" followed by [visited], then the existing len() total. Both lines should show 3.

Add "coffee" as the fourth item in [survey]. Keep the for loop so every item is displayed, then display the new result from len(). The last item line must be "Drink: coffee" and the final line must be "Total drinks: 4".

Store "blue", "green" and "red" in [colours]. Use a for loop and [colour] to display each value after the label "Colour:". After the loop, display "Number of answers:" followed by len(colours). The final line must be "Number of answers: 3".
Repair the wrong loop variable and the missing len() parentheses, then run the corrected survey program.
